REQ-PV-001.title: Codex/agent gets impacted file set without scanning the repo
REQ-PV-001.description: Product goal: a coding agent queries the spec graph and gets a tight {impacted_nodes, impacted_files} answer instead of grepping. Validated empirically in experiments/bench-002 for scoped and cross-domain tasks.

REQ-PV-002.title: Graph is the source of truth; markdown is a regenerated view
REQ-PV-002.description: The graph is stored in .polaris/graph.json and is authoritative. Markdown views are regenerated on demand and never read back.

REQ-PV-003.title: CLI is the only control surface
REQ-PV-003.description: All graph operations are exposed as `pv` subcommands with JSON-by-default output for agents.

REQ-PV-004.title: Asymmetric impact traversal
REQ-PV-004.description: depends_on/implements/uses traverse reverse, affects forward, default depth 3, cycle-safe — produces a tight impact set instead of returning half the codebase.

ENT-PV-NODE.title: SpecNode + Relation + Graph types
ENT-PV-NODE.description: Type contracts for the spec graph: SpecNode (id, type, domain, title, description, tags, relations, createdAt), Relation (type, target), Graph wrapper, Counters, ImpactResult.

ENT-PV-CODEMAP.title: CodeMap (node id → file paths)
ENT-PV-CODEMAP.description: JSON map from node id to file paths. Distinguished at output time from inferred (tag/domain → folder glob) entries so agents don't treat heuristics as ground truth.

ENT-PV-OUTPUT.title: CLI output helpers
ENT-PV-OUTPUT.description: Shared emit/fail helpers used by every command handler. emit() writes JSON to stdout (compact by default, pretty via --pretty); fail() writes a structured error envelope to stderr and exits non-zero.

ENT-PV-IMPACT-RESULT.title: ImpactResult
ENT-PV-IMPACT-RESULT.description: Output of pv impact: { root, depth, impacted_nodes, impacted_files, inferred_files, warnings }.

WF-PV-PERSIST.title: Atomic JSON persistence
WF-PV-PERSIST.description: load → mutate → save via write-temp-then-rename. Used for graph.json, codemap.json, counters.json.

WF-PV-IMPACT.title: Asymmetric impact BFS
WF-PV-IMPACT.description: BFS from root, reverse-traversing depends_on/implements/uses and forward-traversing affects, depth-capped, cycle-safe, dangling targets become non-fatal warnings.

WF-PV-COMPILE.title: Heuristic intent → graph compiler
WF-PV-COMPILE.description: Detect domain by keyword, infer node type from verbs/HTTP-verb prefix, mint stable id, auto-link via shared domain or explicit references. --llm flag is wired but stubbed.

WF-PV-IDS.title: Stable ID minting
WF-PV-IDS.description: Per-(domain,type) counter persisted in .polaris/counters.json. Format: REQ-<DOMAIN>-NNN, API-<DOMAIN>-<SLUG>, etc.

API-PV-GENERATE.title: pv generate <intent>
API-PV-GENERATE.description: Compile a natural-language intent into spec node(s) + auto-relations, save to graph.

API-PV-QUERY.title: pv query <text>
API-PV-QUERY.description: Ranked node match across tag/title/description (tag=3, title=2, description=1).

API-PV-SHOW.title: pv show <id>
API-PV-SHOW.description: Return a single node and its incoming relations as JSON.

API-PV-LINK.title: pv link <fromId> <toId> <relation>
API-PV-LINK.description: Add a typed edge between two existing nodes.

API-PV-IMPACT.title: pv impact <id>
API-PV-IMPACT.description: The headline command. Returns {impacted_nodes, impacted_files, inferred_files, warnings, total_nodes, coverage} for a change at <id>. The coverage field (narrow|broad|global) signals whether the impact set is trustworthy or whether the agent should also fall back to grep. With --files-only, emits just the file paths newline-delimited (no JSON wrapper) for piping into Read loops without narration overhead.

API-PV-EXPORT.title: pv export <id> [--write]
API-PV-EXPORT.description: Render a node as Markdown to stdout, or materialize at .polaris/specs/<id>.md.

API-PV-LIST.title: pv list [--type] [--domain]
API-PV-LIST.description: Enumerate nodes for discovery before targeted query.

API-PV-ADD-FILE.title: pv add-file <id> <path>
API-PV-ADD-FILE.description: Attach a file path to a node in the codemap (Codex calls this after creating a new file).

API-PV-RM-FILE.title: pv rm-file <id> <path>
API-PV-RM-FILE.description: Detach a file path from a node in the codemap.

API-PV-VALIDATE.title: pv validate
API-PV-VALIDATE.description: Verify graph integrity — dangling relation targets, duplicate ids, codemap paths missing on disk, AND orphan source files (files on disk under src/ that aren't referenced by any codemap entry — the leading indicator of a stale graph).

REQ-PV-005.title: Tooling-level PV-vs-grep guidance, not just docs
REQ-PV-005.description: Bench-002 task-3 showed a pure rename refactor (passwordHash → password_hash) costs +65% with PV vs grep. The current mitigation is a CLAUDE.md policy paragraph — fragile, easy for an agent to ignore. PV should provide an advisory command (e.g. `pv suggest <intent>`) that classifies the task shape and tells the agent whether to use PV or grep, returning a structured hint the agent can route on. Source of truth lives in the tool, not in repo docs that drift.

REQ-PV-006.title: One-shot preamble — collapse query+list+impact into a single call
REQ-PV-006.description: Across all bench-002 with-pv runs the agent issued 3 separate PV calls (query, list, impact) before reading any file. Each call is a round-trip plus output narration. A combined `pv ask "<intent>"` (or `pv query --with-impact`) that returns ranked hits AND impact for the top hit in one response would cut the preamble from 3 calls to 1, recovering most of the +12-19% output-token cost we observed in the win cases and shrinking the loss in task-3.

REQ-PV-007.title: Coverage / confidence indicator on impact result
REQ-PV-007.description: `pv impact ENT-PV-NODE` correctly returns nearly every file (a core type underpinning everything), while `pv impact WF-PV-IMPACT` returns 5 — same shape, very different signal density. Today the agent can't tell. Add a `coverage` field (e.g. "narrow" | "broad" | "global") computed from impacted_nodes / total_nodes ratio so the agent knows when to trust the set vs when to also grep. This is exactly the missing signal that would have let task-3 auto-deescalate.

REQ-PV-008.title: Codemap orphan + drift detection in `pv validate`
REQ-PV-008.description: `pv validate` today catches dangling relation targets, duplicate ids, and codemap paths missing on disk. It does NOT catch: (a) source files that exist but aren't referenced by any codemap entry (orphans — the source of stale graphs over time), (b) codemap entries that point at files unchanged for N commits while the graph has been edited (suspected stale relations). Both checks are cheap and would surface drift before it becomes invisible damage.

REQ-PV-009.title: Compact output mode for agents
REQ-PV-009.description: Bench-002 showed with-pv runs emit +12-19% more output tokens than without-pv, primarily from the agent narrating PV's structured output. A `--files-only` flag on `pv impact` (or a `--minimal` mode globally) that returns just `["file1","file2",...]` newline-delimited would let the agent pipe directly into Read without burning tokens on JSON keys. Trade-off: loses the explicit/inferred split — only enable when the agent has already evaluated coverage.

REQ-PV-010.title: Auto-generated human-readable spec/ committed alongside the graph
REQ-PV-010.description: The graph at .polaris/graph.json is JSON-only, hard to scan during code review. A `pv export-all` command should regenerate `spec/<id>.md` for every node plus a `spec/README.md` index (grouped by domain + type, with cross-links). The spec/ directory is tracked in git so PR diffs show spec changes in a human-readable form; staleness is prevented by a CI check (`pv export-all && git diff --quiet spec/`). Not gitignored — being committed is the point.

WF-PV-CLASSIFY.title: Intent → task-shape classifier
WF-PV-CLASSIFY.description: Pattern-based heuristic that decides whether a natural-language intent looks like a rename (use grep), feature add (use PV), refactor (use both), or unknown (default to PV). Implements REQ-PV-005 by encoding the bench-002 finding that grep beats PV for unique-identifier rename tasks.

API-PV-ASK.title: pv ask <intent>
API-PV-ASK.description: One-shot agent preamble: classify the intent shape, search the graph for matching nodes, and run impact analysis on the top hit — all in a single call. Replaces the 3-call query+list+impact preamble that bench-002 measured. Returns the classification with a use_pv/use_grep/use_both recommendation so the agent can route on shape rather than blindly running the PV pipeline. With --minimal, emits a tight {recommendation, reason, root, coverage, files} payload; when recommendation is use_grep, files is empty so the agent learns 'skip PV' with the smallest possible response.

API-PV-EXPORT-ALL.title: pv export-all [--out <dir>]
API-PV-EXPORT-ALL.description: Regenerate the entire human-readable spec from the graph: one Markdown file per node plus a README.md index grouped by domain and type. Default output directory is ./spec. Cross-links between related nodes are emitted as relative .md links so the result browses naturally on GitHub.
